assumptions.text: Jev (TypeSafe) HTTP contract is assumed, not verified: POST {base_url}/v1/evaluate with {state, questions, version} and Bearer auth, returning {answers: {id: {value, confidence, index}}}. Only core.orchestrator.decisions.JevClient depends on it; verify against TypeSafe's API docs before connecting a real key.
Resolved: the Jev HTTP contract is no longer assumed; see KNOWLEDGE-205fb661 (verified from the TypeSafe API reference, implemented in M1-06b).

decisions.title: Cloud platform: AWS
decisions.text: The system runs on AWS (EKS, KMS, Secrets Manager, S3, RDS Postgres) in US and EU regions; Cedar authorization fits AWS natively. Chosen by the human during SPEC-1 discovery.

decisions.title: LLM provider: Anthropic Claude for mid and frontier tiers
decisions.text: Mid-tier and frontier tiers (CR-D1) use Anthropic Claude models; the third tier is the self-hosted open-weights model per region (RP-D4). The EV judge must come from a different model family (EV-Q3).

decisions.title: Delivery: ordered milestones
decisions.text: All 15 components plus orchestration are in scope; delivery is in ordered milestones, each a set of bounded tasks, defined in the plan.

decisions.title: Success for first production release: launch baseline
decisions.text: No numeric business targets at launch. Success = the EV-D5 release gate passes and the 8 framework scenarios pass end to end; business targets (deflection, CSAT, FCR) are set after one month of production data.

decisions.title: v1 runtime: learning deployment profile (one free VM + free managed services)
decisions.text: This is a learning project, not sold to businesses. The 79 ADPs remain the target design (AWS, US/EU regions, Kubernetes, GPUs). v1 runs on one Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM VM (Docker Compose: Temporal dev server + workers, orchestrator, API, Qdrant or Qdrant Cloud, Jaeger, OpenBao, Ollama) plus free managed services (Vercel frontend, Neon/Supabase Postgres, Qdrant Cloud, Cloudflare R2, Upstash Redis, Grafana Cloud/Langfuse, Hugging Face Spaces for the Streamlit console, GitHub Actions). LLMs: Claude mid/frontier under a hard spend cap, Groq/Gemini free tiers and Ollama for the third tier, judge and screening. Total monthly spend cap: USD 50 (provider spend limits). Every requirement is satisfied in its v1 form per the SPEC.md profile table.
decisions.source: user choice 2026-10-09; cost analysis in session

decisions.title: v1 runtime: learning deployment profile, USD 10/month cap
decisions.text: Same learning deployment profile as DECISION-b4cdefcc (one Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM VM with Docker Compose + free managed services; the 79 ADPs remain the production target), with the total monthly spend cap lowered from USD 50 to USD 10 by the human. Free tiers (Groq / Gemini, or Ollama) serve easy and mid-difficulty turns, the fallback, judge and screening; Claude serves only the hardest turns under a USD 10 console spend limit, falling back to the best free model when the limit is reached.

decisions.title: Module-owned schema
decisions.text: Chosen by Intelligent_developer_123 (2026-10-12): no remaining task may change migrations/, so each task keeps its tables' SQL in its own in-scope module and applies it through the schema_migrations ledger from M0-03 (data.migrate.psql). migrations/ holds only the M0-03 base schema. Every new tenant table still gets forced RLS, a tenant_isolation-style policy, app_owner ownership and explicit grants.

knowledge.title: Design source of truth
knowledge.text: Binding design lives in docs/decisions/checkpoint.md (decision log §3, reasoning per component), docs/decisions/adp_groups.yaml (230 decisions grouped into 79 ADPs) and one detailed document per ADP in docs/decisions/adp/. SPEC.md requirements map one-to-one to ADPs.

knowledge.title: Run gates with the project venv on PATH
knowledge.text: On this machine 'python' on PATH resolves to another tool's venv (hermes-agent) without pytest. The project venv is .venv (Python 3.12, pip install -e .[dev]); run Genesis gates as PATH="$PWD/.venv/Scripts:$PATH" genesis gate . <task>. Never install project deps into the hermes venv.

knowledge.title: Approval shorthand
knowledge.text: Intelligent_developer_123 (2026-10-14): when a review is requested and the human replies 'continue', record the independent-review approval with --human Intelligent_developer_123 --reason 'I approve'. Only an actual 'continue' reply from the human counts; never record an approval without one.

knowledge.title: Jev (TypeSafe System One) API contract
knowledge.text: Verified from TypeSafe docs (Quick start + API reference, given by the user 2026-10-15): POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, Bearer auth, body {state: string|object|array, model: 'jev-latest', questions: {id: {type: choice|score|noul, instructions, criteria}}}; choice criteria = {option: description|null} (max 255), score criteria = ordered list (2-10 levels), noul criteria optional {true, false}. Answers: choice {choice, probabilities, confidence}, score {score (weighted, between levels), legend, probabilities, confidence}, noul {noul 0-1, no confidence}; response also has model and usage. Errors: 400/401/413/415/422 = our request or key is wrong; 429/529 = retry with backoff. Implemented in core.orchestrator.decisions (M1-06b).

notes: Turns table SQL in src/channels/api/turns.py (DECISION-d4b79fe1). Duplicate = same (tenant, principal, conversation, Idempotency-Key). Message text is not stored: handed to dispatch inside the insert transaction (rollback on failure). SSE: replay via EventLog, expired -> status stream_expired + transcript as final{history:true}, then live polling of the event log with heartbeat comments. Sign-in, dispatch and transcript are create_app() parameters so later tasks plug in.

tasks.next_action: Human independent review of src/channels/identity/, src/channels/sessions.py, tests/identity/
notes: Ed25519 JWTs via cryptography. Access tokens 24 h (UA-D9) but honoured only while the session is live and matches the token's sub+tier; on-behalf-of tokens 15 min per UA-ADP-02 (SPEC FR-7 wording says OBO 24 h - flagged to the user). Tables (sessions, conversations, cases, otp_challenges) are module-owned. channels.identity.server.build_app wires sign-in into the M1-01 API; python -m channels.identity serve runs it with a mock IdP.
limitations: No server-side nonce store: a captured mock-IdP ID token can be replayed within its 5-minute life; dev keys are generated at start (no IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY loading yet); OTP delivery is a callable (dev prints codes); no rate limit on otp/start yet (RP-ADP-01); an open event stream only touches the session at connect, so a stream outlives an expired or logged-out session (KK3, needs channels/api changes); case linking by Jev choice + user confirmation (MS-Q1) is not here.

notes: Static page, no build step, no npm dependencies. tasks.next_action: Human independent review of src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py, planner.py, src/schemas/, tests/orchestrator/
notes: Thread state is a TypedDict of plain JSON values (safe checkpoint deserialization) with schema_version + MIGRATIONS registry; unknown versions escalate (MS-D13). One node per ADP-01 stage; every entry checked against TRANSITIONS, any non-terminal stage may trip to ESCALATED_HITL. Waits end the run and the next event resumes it; approval resumed after > 1 h calls revalidate before acting (MS-D18). Scoped ReAct is one step per graph cycle (checkpointed), max 4 steps / 2 critiques / read-only tools. Postgres checkpointer via PostgresSaver.setup().
limitations: Decisions are hooks (fakes in tests) until Jev triage (ADP-05), slot filling, the SOP registry and the LLM ReAct step exist; no idempotency fence around side effects yet (MS-D9, tool layer); no blob externalization (MS-D7); checkpoint tables are library-owned without row-level security (thread id = tenant:case, access only through the orchestrator); Plan-and-Solve DAG depth and the Jev resolution check before RESOLVED are not built; the approval threshold defaults to 1000 rather than reading tenant_settings; no Temporal outer saga (ADP-02).

tasks.outcome: M1 Core: Temporal ticket workflow with activities running LangGraph turns and approval / cancel signals

scenarios.observable: a waiting workflow survives a worker restart and resumes on a signal

tasks.next_action: Human independent review of src/workflows/ and tests/workflows/
notes: TicketWorkflow (stdlib + temporalio only, sandbox-safe) keeps ids/status; each turn runs the statechart in the run_turn activity with a per-turn event id stored in the thread state, so a retry resumes the crashed turn from its checkpoint and a repeated finished turn applies nothing twice; a pending turn from another run fails non-retryably. Signals reply / decide / cancel; query state; 24 h reply and 48 h approval timers (inputs, shortened in tests). Tests run against the compose Temporal and Postgres.
limitations: Customer text passes through Temporal history (activity input, reply signal) until a transcript store lets turns carry message ids; reply/approval timeouts end the workflow without telling the LangGraph state (no timeout event in the statechart); no saga compensations yet (TA-ADP-05; the statechart only changes things after approval); the API's dispatch hook is not wired to start_ticket yet; a resolved ticket ends its workflow, so a later message needs a new start; no worker entrypoint, only the worker() helper.

tasks.outcome: M1 Core: Jev decision client and question sets with masked input and a fallback LLM classifier

tasks.next_action: Human independent review of src/core/orchestrator/decisions.py, triage.py, tests/decisions/
notes: DecisionEngine: versioned question sets (QUESTIONS_VERSION), Masked-only input with an egress PII re-scan, numbers/money refused in question text, answers validated against the question type (invalid = Jev down). Gates: triage (triage.py maps intent+severity to acuity, SOP intents get an sop_name), guards (confident yes or no), tool selection (shortlist or None). Jev down: triage uses llm_fallback(complete) with confidence capped at 0.89 so an SOP never auto-runs on a fallback guess; both down -> ask the customer; guards -> no; tools -> none.
limitations: Jev HTTP contract assumed (ASSUMPTION recorded); masking is an interim regex pass until the token vault (SG-ADP-02); thresholds are code defaults, not per-route YAML calibrated on golden sets; no Langfuse telemetry of decisions yet; llm_fallback takes any complete(prompt) callable - no model provider wired; triage_hook is not yet wired into a running orchestrator.

tasks.outcome: M1 Core: slot-budget context assembler with token counting, provider prompt caching and passage compression

tasks.next_action: Human independent review of src/core/context/ and tests/context/
notes: assemble(): five slots at 15/15/35/25/10 % of the window (16,384 default), checked after rendering; system+tools is the cached prefix and a build error if too big; pins verbatim, least important left out; passages top 5 by score, delimited, compressed to the room left, dropped if still too big; dialogue newest turns verbatim (max 6, contiguous) then the rolling summary; scratchpad newest first. to_anthropic() puts cache_control on the prefix block only, alternates roles, scratchpad last. Spotlight delimiters defuse spoofed markers. budget.status(): turn budgets 4k/8k/16k minus cascade reserve, wrap-up at 90 %, hand-off at 50k/24 h.

notes: JevClient now speaks the documented API (KNOWLEDGE-205fb661): POST /v1/systemone with {state as object, model, id-keyed questions}; answers parsed per type into one Answer (choice; score -> most likely level from probabilities; noul -> yes/no at 0.5 with that side's probability). 429/529 retried once after a back-off; 400/401/413/415/422 raise JevRejected (logged as a configuration error, still fail-safe); other failures JevUnavailable.
